62:The side panel slides in from the board's right as it opens, in the same quick motion, the board narrowing alongside it, and slides back out to the right as it closes, the board widening as it goes; replacing what it holds with another story, drafting, or research changes its content in place, with no slide. Its content, and focus in it, are there as soon as it starts to open.
63:Every motion here takes about 150 milliseconds, never longer, and a move made while another is still under way starts from wherever the card is then, never queued behind it.

66-
67-Next sprint can start on its own: a "Start automatically" switch on Next sprint's heading, beside Send sprint, its tooltip saying the next sprint starts as soon as the current one is done. It starts off, and is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, so it is kept across reloads and restarts.
68-While it is on, once every story of Current sprint has ended Done, the current sprint closes by itself, as Close sprint closes it, and Next sprint, if it holds a story, is sent at once, as Send sprint sends it, with nobody having to start it; and while no sprint is current, a story added to an empty Next sprint starts it the same way. 74-
75-The stories, their order, and which section each is in are saved with the project's data, as the [ProjectData](../project-data/index.md#project-data) says, in `.suspense/planning/`, a file per story, holding its hidden anchor as a queued prompt's is, and an `order.json` listing the sections and their stories, so the plan is kept with the project and comes back as it was left. A story's steps are saved in its own file, in their order, as its steps say, never apart from it.

77-## Steps
78-
79-A story can have steps: one or more further prompts, each a piece of the story done after the one before, as a chain's steps are. Each step has a prompt, a mode of its own, Code or Spec, starting as the story's, and a model and effort, starting as the story's, and may have attachments. A story with no steps is just its own prompt, as before; its prompt is always its first step.
80-An open story lists its steps beneath its prompt, in order, each a row numbered from 2, the story's own prompt being 1, with its mode pill and the first line of its prompt, opening in place to edit, as a story does. The story's own prompt stays first and can't be moved among them.
81-A step belongs to its story and to nothing else. It is saved in the story's file, in a `steps` list of the story's hidden anchor, in its order, and saved as every change to the plan is, straight away; a story duplicated copies its steps, and one deleted deletes them. Its order is kept wherever the story goes, between sections, into a sprint, and back from Done.

A story sent can't be given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they were sent. In Current sprint, a story with steps lists its steps on its card, beneath its title, a line for each step, in order, each with its number, the first line of its prompt cut off with an ellipsis, and its own status, as a running chain's are in the Tasks tab; in Done, and in a finding started from the story, its steps are listed the same way, collapsed to its step count until it is expanded. The same steps, in the same order, are what every place shows, since every place reads them from the story's own file.
83-A step is only ever added to a story that exists. Adding one to a story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited, or by another window, or whose file was removed from `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

Each column is headed as above, so nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open story, a drafting or research panel, and the citations and steps inside a story all use the same five parts, below.

96-Everything in Planning is built from five parts, each always drawn the same way, in the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode:

# Planning

## How To Build

A Planning should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A Planning should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, integration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [Theme](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Sprint

Stories move between the Backlog and Next sprint by dragging, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, a card dragged by its grip from one column into a gap in the other as within either, the gap opened in the column the pointer is over, as motion says; an empty one takes a drop at its top. Dragged near the board's left or right edge, the board scrolls sideways, and near a column's top or bottom, that column scrolls, as dragging says. Only the Backlog and Next sprint take drops: Current sprint and Done open no gap, a story dropped on them stays where it was, and their cards can't be picked up, nor can a finding. Stories move too from a card's menu, "Move to next sprint" or "Move to backlog". Their order within Next sprint is the order they will be sent. A card's menu also has "Duplicate" and "Delete".
"Send sprint", a primary button at the right of Next sprint's heading, enabled while it holds a story, sends every story in it, in order, as though each had been written in the chat input on its mode's tab and sent, one after another, as the [PromptSending](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending) says: each task queues in its lane behind the one before it, in the order of the sprint, and each question runs at once. The stories go into the queue as one block, so nothing sent later comes between them, and the queue's auto-send carries them on as ever, as the [QueueList](../prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list) says.
Each story starts a conversation of its own, as though New conversation had been pressed just before it, and so does each later step of a story's chain: a story never carries on the conversation of the story before it, nor of anything its lane ran before the sprint. New conversation, pressed before the sprint was sent, is left for the next prompt written in the chat input.
A story can't be sent on its own. The only way a story reaches work is through the sprint: a story in the Backlog waits until it is moved into Next sprint and the sprint is sent, and a story in Next sprint goes when the sprint does. Nothing in Planning, its cards, their menus, the open story, the keyboard, the palette, or the ribbon, sends a single story, and nothing elsewhere sends a story by any other route: a story can't be dragged or copied into the chat input or the queue to be sent from there, and its menu has no "Send" or "Edit in chat input". The chat input's own prompts are not stories and are sent as ever; once a prompt is a story, the sprint is its only way to work. To send one story at once, it is the only story in Next sprint when Send sprint is pressed. A story that failed or was cancelled is sent again the same way, with the next sprint.
Sending the sprint moves its stories into the "Current sprint" column, to the right of Next sprint, so Next sprint is empty again and stories added meanwhile go there, to be the sprint after. Current sprint and Done are columns of the board whatever they hold, never appearing, disappearing, or collapsing; while no sprint is under way Current sprint is empty and shows its empty state, as Done does before anything is done. A story in Current sprint keeps its place, its card showing its task's status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking it opens its task in the Tasks tab; it can't be moved or edited there. Once every story of Current sprint has ended, its column's heading offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done into the Done column, their cards muted, and those that failed, were cancelled, or stopped to the start of Next sprint, in their order, to be sent again. While a sprint is current, Send sprint is disabled, its tooltip saying a sprint is already under way.
Send sprint only ever moves into Current sprint the stories it actually sent. A story with nothing to send, its title and its prompt both empty, is skipped: it stays in Next sprint, where it was, and Send sprint's result says, muted, how many it skipped and why, as "1 empty story left in Next sprint". A sprint where every story is empty sends nothing and makes no Current sprint.
Once a sprint is done, it can always be closed. Every story of Current sprint counts as ended once its task has ended, done, failed, cancelled, or stopped, or once its task can no longer be found, as when its record was deleted, it was never recorded, or the application quit before it was. A story whose task is missing is never shown as Queued, or as anything still to come: its card reads "Task missing", muted, in the theme's warning colour, its tooltip saying its task can't be found, and it counts as ended and not Done. A story still waiting in its lane's queue, or held for review, as the paused section says, is still to come and hasn't ended. So Close sprint shows as soon as no story of Current sprint is building, compiling, running, paused, queued, or held, and never waits on a task that can't arrive.
Close sprint treats a story whose task is missing as it treats one that failed or was cancelled: it goes back to the start of Next sprint, with the others sent again, in their order, never into Done. Closing saves the sections, Done, Next sprint, the Backlog, and the emptied Current sprint, to `order.json` straight away, as the [ProjectData](../project-data/index.md#project-data) says, and Current sprint's state is worked out afresh from the stories' tasks whenever the plan is read, so a sprint that finished, or whose tasks went missing, before a reload or a restart can still be closed after it, as before.

## Motion

Dragging a card on the board feels as it does in Trello, and the board opens the gap, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) lets its user do, in place of the accent line alone. Only the board's cards move this way; steps in an open story, and every other list, are dragged as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, with its line.
A card picked up by its grip lifts off the board as a full-size copy of itself, the same width and height, drawn as the parts draw a story card, tilted a few degrees, about 3, on the theme's overlay surface with its edge border and the soft shadow the [Theme](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme)'s elevation gives floating surfaces, the one shadow on the board. It follows the pointer, held where it was grabbed, and never takes the mouse. The card's own place in its column becomes the gap it left, empty, the card's height, so the column doesn't jump as it lifts.
Where the card would land, the cards slide apart to open a placeholder the dragged card's height, 8 pixels from the cards either side, as the cards are spaced: a box the card's size on the theme's well surface, with its corners rounded 6 pixels as a card's are, and no border, so it reads as an empty slot. The gap is chosen as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) chooses it, among the cards of the column the pointer is over, and only one is open at a time: as the pointer moves into another gap, or another column, the gap it left closes as the new one opens, and the gap the card came from closes once the pointer leaves its column, opening again if it comes back. A column that takes no drops opens no gap, and its cards never move while a card is dragged over it.
Nothing waits on motion while the user is waiting on it. The gap the card would drop into is updated at once, the moment the pointer crosses the middle of a card, exactly as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, and a drop always goes where the gap was chosen, even while the cards are still sliding toward it; only the sliding of the cards around it is animated, quickly, as below.
Dropped over an open gap, the copy settles into it: it straightens, its shadow fades, and it moves from where it was released into the placeholder, which it then is, the story saved in its new place at the moment of the drop, as every change to the plan is. Dropped anywhere else, or where it began, it settles back into the gap it came from the same way, and nothing changes. Escape while dragging cancels it, settling the card back where it was.
A card moved any other way animates to its new place, in Linear's

### Style

a quick motion of about 150 milliseconds, eased out, sliding

from where it was to where it now is, the cards it passes or leaves sliding to close and open the room it takes, never fading or bouncing. That covers every move the sprint describes: "Move to next sprint" and "Move to backlog" from a card's menu, Alt+Up, Alt+Down, Alt+Left, and Alt+Right, Ctrl+Enter, Send sprint moving its stories into Current sprint, and Close sprint moving them into Done and back to the start of Next sprint. A card added, as by a composer or Duplicate, slides the cards below it down to make room, and a card deleted slides them up to close it, in the same motion. 11:## Indicator
12-
13:The indicator is a line 2 pixels thick in the [Theme](../../theme/index.md#theme)'s accent, with rounded ends and a small open circle, 6 pixels across and in the same colour, at its leading end. It lies across the gap, centred on the gap, horizontal between the rows of a list, running the list's width less its padding, and vertical between the tabs of a tab bar or the items of a row, running their height. It is drawn over the items, taking no room of its own, so nothing moves to make space while the drag is under way, and it never takes the mouse.
14:A user may open the gap instead, as its user says: the items either side slide apart to make room where the item would land, and what that user says of the gap, the dragged copy, and the drop holds there in place of what is said here.
15-
16-## Choosing The Gap
17-
18:Which gap is shown follows the pointer: over the first half of an item, the gap before it; over the second half, the gap after it, halves taken along the direction the items run. Past the last item, the gap after it; before the first, the gap before it. The two gaps either side of the dragged item itself are where it already is, so neither shows an indicator, and dropping there changes nothing. A gap an item may not be dropped into, as its user says, shows no indicator either, and nothing is marked while the pointer is over it.
19:The indicator moves from gap to gap at once as the pointer crosses the middle of an item, with no animation, so it is always exactly where a drop would land.
20-
21-## Between Lists
22-
23:Where its user lets items move between lists, as the columns of a board, an item is dragged from one list into a gap of another as it is within its own. The gap is chosen, as above, among the items of the list the pointer is over, and the indicator is drawn across that list, running its width less its padding, never across the list the item came from. A list with no items has one gap, at its top, so an empty list takes a drop there, the indicator drawn across its top beneath its heading. A list its user says takes no drops shows no indicator anywhere over it, and an item dropped on it goes nowhere; its own items can't be picked up to be dragged.

31-Items that scroll can be reordered past what is in view, so an item can be dragged to any gap, however long the list. While an item is dragged, held near an edge of the scrolling area the items run along, within 32 pixels of its top or bottom for a list, or of its left or right for a row, the area scrolls that way on its own, slowly at first and faster the nearer the pointer is to the edge, or the further past it, up to about a row every 50 milliseconds, smoothly frame by frame rather than in jumps, and stops at its end. Moving the pointer away from the edge stops it at once. The wheel and trackpad scroll the area too while the item is dragged, as they do at any time, without dropping it.
32:However the area scrolls, the dragged copy stays under the pointer, and the gap shown is chosen anew each frame from where the pointer is over the items now there, so the indicator is always exactly where a drop would land. An area that doesn't scroll, or holds every item in view, doesn't scroll on its own.

content.text:
Dragging a card on Planning's board now works the Trello way, and other moves slide into place the Linear way. I couldn't build the real tree, though. I checked the code in a temporary copy, where it compiles and 19 of 23 Planning tests pass. None of the 4 failures are in the code I changed.

**What changed:**
- **Pick-up:** grabbing a card lifts a full-size copy from where you grabbed it. The copy sits on the overlay surface with its edge border and the theme's floating shadow, and it doesn't take clicks.
- **The gap:** the card's own place stays open until the pointer leaves its column. Where it would land, a placeholder opens: the card's height, 8 px from its neighbours, on the well surface with 6 px corners. The others close at the same time, and Current sprint and Done open nothing. The board no longer draws the accent line; steps in an open story keep it.
- **Nothing waits:** the gap is still chosen at once as the pointer moves. Only the cards around it slide.
- **Dropping:** dropped on a gap, the copy straightens, its shadow fades, and it settles into the placeholder. Dropped anywhere else, or on Escape, it settles back and nothing changes.
- **Other moves:** anything that reorders the plan slides cards to their new place in 150 ms, eased out. That covers the card menu, Alt+arrows, Ctrl+Enter, Send sprint, Close sprint, adding and deleting. Focus and saving still happen at once, and a new move starts from wherever a card is mid-slide.
- **Side panel:** it slides in from the right and back out, with the board narrowing and widening alongside. Swapping what it shows doesn't slide.

The sliding and tilt pieces are new shared files, `src/animations/slide.rs` and `src/animations/tilt.rs`. The rest is in `src/planning.rs`.

**Where the code falls short of the spec:**
- **The tilt is faked.** GPUI can't rotate boxes or text, so the copy is drawn as narrow strips stepped down by about 3°. The top and bottom edges slope, but the left and right edges stay upright.
- **The side panel closes empty.** When it slides out, its content goes at once and only its empty surface slides away.

**Why I couldn't build the real tree:**
- `src/prompt_mode.rs` has another session's half-finished edit around line 3958 that doesn't compile.
- The sandbox won't let the build read `.suspense/system-prompts/*.md`.

I worked around both only in the temporary copy and didn't touch either in the repo.

**The 4 failing tests:**
- Two break in the unchanged `render_composer`, whose `test_support` call has no element id.
- One counts citations against the current spec.
- One is about newline handling in the drafting input.

I also added a test case that a dragged card's own old place never counts when choosing the gap.

To keep tests predictable, all motion finishes instantly under test. Without that, a test that clicks in the side panel right after opening it missed, because the panel hadn't slid in yet.
